CaKind.description: Certificate authority that signs HTTPS certificates for lane hostnames.
enumDescriptions: devlanes creates its own CA in `~/.devlanes/ca` on first use, limited to names under `localhost`, `test`, `internal`, `home.arpa` and `hostnames.tld`, so it cannot sign for real sites. Trust it once with `devlanes certs trust`.

Load mkcert's existing root CA (from `mkcert -CAROOT`) instead, so browsers that already trust it need nothing new. HTTPS stays off when `mkcert` is not on `PATH`; the mkcert CA has no name limits, and `certs untrust` leaves it trusted.

tld.description: Top-level domain for the `resolver` strategy, such as `test`; required there. A new devlanes CA may sign names under the `tld` set when it is created, whatever the strategy, so switching to another `tld` later needs a new CA.

LogRetention.description: Limits for stored service output; reaching either one deletes the oldest output first.
LogRetention.markdownDescription: Limits for stored service output; reaching either one deletes the oldest output first.

days.description: Delete output older than this many days, along with its index entries in the database; defaults to 7 and must be at least 1. The newest log file of each stopped service is kept.

max_size.description: Total size of stored output across all projects and lanes; defaults to `5GiB` and must be above zero. Over it, the oldest output goes first wherever it is, but each stopped service's newest file and up to 1 MiB of a running service's current file are kept.
max_size.markdownDescription: Total size of stored output across all projects and lanes; defaults to `5GiB` and must be above zero. Over it, the oldest output goes first wherever it is, but each stopped service's newest file and up to 1 MiB of a running service's current file are kept.

LogsConfig.markdownDescription: Retention of the service output stored under `~/.devlanes/logs`.

retention.markdownDescription: Age and total-size limits for stored service output; a cleanup every 10 minutes deletes the oldest output past either one. Defaults to 7 days and `5GiB`.

ProxyConfig.description: Ports and network exposure of the daemon's proxy, which routes each lane hostname to its service.
ProxyConfig.markdownDescription: Ports and network exposure of the daemon's proxy, which routes each lane hostname to its service.

http_port.description: Port for plain HTTP; defaults to 80, falling back to 8080 like `https_port`, and must differ from it. While HTTPS runs it redirects known hostnames to HTTPS; without a CA it serves them over plain HTTP.
http_port.markdownDescription: Port for plain HTTP; defaults to 80, falling back to 8080 like `https_port`, and must differ from it. While HTTPS runs it redirects known hostnames to HTTPS; without a CA it serves them over plain HTTP.

https_port.description: Port the HTTPS proxy listens on; defaults to 443. When the port is taken or not allowed (low ports on Linux need extra permission), the daemon falls back to 8443 and service URLs carry the port.
https_port.markdownDescription: Port the HTTPS proxy listens on; defaults to 443. When the port is taken or not allowed (low ports on Linux need extra permission), the daemon falls back to 8443 and service URLs carry the port.

lan.description: Accept connections from other devices on the network; defaults to false, which refuses every peer that is not this machine. Those devices must still resolve the hostnames to this machine and trust the CA.
lan.markdownDescription: Accept connections from other devices on the network; defaults to false, which refuses every peer that is not this machine. Those devices must still resolve the hostnames to this machine and trust the CA.

via.description: Add `Via: 1.1 devlanes.run` to every response the proxy forwards from a service (`1.1 devlanes.run (remote)` for lanes on a remote box), so a client can tell that devlanes sat in between. Defaults to true; set false if a client or test compares response headers exactly.

Resolver.description: Strategy that makes lane hostnames resolve to this machine.
enumDescriptions: Lane domains end in `.localhost` (`acme.localhost`, `acme-2.localhost`), which browsers and many system resolvers send to loopback by themselves. `hosts_file` covers programs that do not.

Keep `.localhost` names and always write exact hostnames to `/etc/hosts`, as `hosts_file: always` does, whatever `hosts_file` says; a project's `lanes.hosts_file` still takes precedence. Needs the helper from `devlanes certs trust --hosts`.

Lane domains become `<project>.<tld>` and `<project>-<N>.<tld>`, answered by a DNS server the daemon runs on `127.0.0.1:15353`, so wildcard hostnames resolve too for programs that use the system resolver. Needs `tld` and a one-time `devlanes certs trust --resolver`; projects that set `lanes.vars.domain` or `lanes.matrix` keep their own domains.
Reserved for public DNS names with DNS-01 certificates; not supported yet, so the config is rejected.
Resolver.markdownDescription: Strategy that makes lane hostnames resolve to this machine.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Lane domains end in `.localhost` (`acme.localhost`, `acme-2.localhost`), which browsers and many system resolvers send to loopback by themselves. `hosts_file` covers programs that do not.

Keep `.localhost` names and always write exact hostnames to `/etc/hosts`, as `hosts_file: always` does, whatever `hosts_file` says; a project's `lanes.hosts_file` still takes precedence. Needs the helper from `devlanes certs trust --hosts`.

Lane domains become `<project>.<tld>` and `<project>-<N>.<tld>`, answered by a DNS server the daemon runs on `127.0.0.1:15353`, so wildcard hostnames resolve too for programs that use the system resolver. Needs `tld` and a one-time `devlanes certs trust --resolver`; projects that set `lanes.vars.domain` or `lanes.matrix` keep their own domains.
Reserved for public DNS names with DNS-01 certificates; not supported yet, so the config is rejected.

StartConfig.description: What a plain `devlanes start`, or `s` on a lane in the TUI, starts. Changes apply to the next command.
StartConfig.markdownDescription: What a plain `devlanes start`, or `s` on a lane in the TUI, starts. Changes apply to the next command.

restore.description: Bring back the services the lane ran before, with the same profiles, so a reboot or daemon crash costs one `devlanes start`; defaults to true. A lane stopped as a whole with `devlanes stop` has nothing to bring back and starts its `default` profile. Set false to always start the `default` profile (or every `autostart` service). `lane resume` and `daemon restart` restore either way.
restore.markdownDescription: Bring back the services the lane ran before, with the same profiles, so a reboot or daemon crash costs one `devlanes start`; defaults to true. A lane stopped as a whole with `devlanes stop` has nothing to bring back and starts its `default` profile. Set false to always start the `default` profile (or every `autostart` service). `lane resume` and `daemon restart` restore either way.

StartupConfig.description: Pacing of service starts, shared by every lane and project on this machine. Starts queue first come, first served; only spawning waits, running processes are never limited.
StartupConfig.markdownDescription: Pacing of service starts, shared by every lane and project on this machine. Starts queue first come, first served; only spawning waits, running processes are never limited.

initial.description: Adaptive starting window; defaults to `max`, so starts run at full speed until the machine is under pressure. Set it lower to ramp up from a few slots instead; never above `max`.
initial.markdownDescription: Adaptive starting window; defaults to `max`, so starts run at full speed until the machine is under pressure. Set it lower to ramp up from a few slots instead; never above `max`.

max.description: Most services starting at once: the constant window in `fixed` mode and the ceiling in `adaptive` mode. Defaults to the number of CPU cores; `all` ignores it.
max.markdownDescription: Most services starting at once: the constant window in `fixed` mode and the ceiling in `adaptive` mode. Defaults to the number of CPU cores; `all` ignores it.

mode.description: `adaptive`, `fixed` or `all`; default `adaptive`. A starting service holds its slot until its ready check (`tcp`, `http`, `log` or `cmd`) passes, it fails, or `slot_timeout` passes; one without a check (`ready: started`) holds it until it settles (`settle_cpu`).
mode.markdownDescription: `adaptive`, `fixed` or `all`; default `adaptive`. A starting service holds its slot until its ready check (`tcp`, `http`, `log` or `cmd`) passes, it fails, or `slot_timeout` passes; one without a check (`ready: started`) holds it until it settles (`settle_cpu`).

reserve_memory.description: Free memory every new start must leave, on top of the memory the services already starting are expected to still need (each one's past startup peak, or 512 MiB without history). Defaults to 10% of RAM, at most `2GiB`; `0B` turns it off. A start with nothing else starting never waits for it. `all` ignores it.
reserve_memory.markdownDescription: Free memory every new start must leave, on top of the memory the services already starting are expected to still need (each one's past startup peak, or 512 MiB without history). Defaults to 10% of RAM, at most `2GiB`; `0B` turns it off. A start with nothing else starting never waits for it. `all` ignores it.

settle_cpu.description: Only for services without a ready check (`ready: started`, the default for a service without `hosts`): such a service gives its slot back once its process tree uses less than this share of one core for 2 s, meaning it has finished starting up. Services with a `tcp`, `http`, `log` or `cmd` check keep their slot until the check passes instead. Defaults to `10%`.
settle_cpu.markdownDescription: Only for services without a ready check (`ready: started`, the default for a service without `hosts`): such a service gives its slot back once its process tree uses less than this share of one core for 2 s, meaning it has finished starting up. Services with a `tcp`, `http`, `log` or `cmd` check keep their slot until the check passes instead. Defaults to `10%`.

slot_timeout.description: Longest a starting service holds its slot; after it, the next queued service may start even if this one is not ready, so services waiting on each other cannot block the queue. Defaults to `20s` and must be above zero; the service itself keeps starting.
slot_timeout.markdownDescription: Longest a starting service holds its slot; after it, the next queued service may start even if this one is not ready, so services waiting on each other cannot block the queue. Defaults to `20s` and must be above zero; the service itself keeps starting.

target_cpu.description: System CPU use below which `adaptive` mode adds slots; defaults to `75%`, and must be above 0% and at most 100%. Lower it to keep the machine responsive during large starts; other modes ignore it.
target_cpu.markdownDescription: System CPU use below which `adaptive` mode adds slots; defaults to `75%`, and must be above 0% and at most 100%. Lower it to keep the machine responsive during large starts; other modes ignore it.

StartupMode.description: How the number of services allowed to start at once is chosen.
enumDescriptions: Begin each burst of starts at `initial` (by default `max`, full speed). Halve the slots after 3 s above 90% CPU or when the system reports memory pressure, start nothing while that pressure is critical, and add a slot every 2 s while system CPU stays below `target_cpu`, up to `max`.
Allow `max` starts at a time, never more or fewer. A start also waits while free memory cannot fit what it needs.
Start every service immediately, with no limit and no memory check.
StartupMode.markdownDescription: How the number of services allowed to start at once is chosen.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Begin each burst of starts at `initial` (by default `max`, full speed). Halve the slots after 3 s above 90% CPU or when the system reports memory pressure, start nothing while that pressure is critical, and add a slot every 2 s while system CPU stays below `target_cpu`, up to `max`.
Allow `max` starts at a time, never more or fewer. A start also waits while free memory cannot fit what it needs.
Start every service immediately, with no limit and no memory check.

StateConfig.description: Size budget for the daemon's SQLite database, enforced by its hourly cleanup.
StateConfig.markdownDescription: Size budget for the daemon's SQLite database, enforced by its hourly cleanup.

max_size.description: Size the database (`state.db` with its WAL and shared-memory files) should stay under; defaults to `512MiB` and must be above zero. When it is larger, the cleanup deletes the oldest metric samples first, then the oldest history (finished runs, log index entries, remote boxes), even before their retention ends. Lanes, ports and running units are never deleted, so the file can stay above the budget.
max_size.markdownDescription: Size the database (`state.db` with its WAL and shared-memory files) should stay under; defaults to `512MiB` and must be above zero. When it is larger, the cleanup deletes the oldest metric samples first, then the oldest history (finished runs, log index entries, remote boxes), even before their retention ends. Lanes, ports and running units are never deleted, so the file can stay above the budget.

TerminalConfig.description: Terminal integration of the CLI, or a terminal app name from older versions, which is ignored.
TerminalConfig.markdownDescription: Terminal integration of the CLI, or a terminal app name from older versions, which is ignored.

enumDescriptions: Only in terminals known to support it, on human output to a terminal; never inside tmux, screen, CI or a dumb terminal.
In every terminal, tmux included; a terminal without support may ignore it, or keep a title devlanes cannot put back.
Never use it.
TerminalFeature.markdownDescription: When devlanes uses a terminal feature (title, links, notifications, marks).
markdownEnumDescriptions: Only in terminals known to support it, on human output to a terminal; never inside tmux, screen, CI or a dumb terminal.

TerminalProgress.description: When start progress goes to the terminal tab's progress bar.
enumDescriptions: Only in terminals known to draw it (Ghostty, WezTerm, iTerm2 3.6.6+, Windows Terminal, ConEmu, Ptyxis 48+, Konsole 26.04+); never inside tmux, screen, CI or a dumb terminal.

In every terminal, for ones `auto` does not recognize such as kitty; a terminal without support may ignore it or show it as text or a notification. Inside tmux it is passed through, which needs `allow-passthrough on`.
Never draw the progress bar.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Only in terminals known to draw it (Ghostty, WezTerm, iTerm2 3.6.6+, Windows Terminal, ConEmu, Ptyxis 48+, Konsole 26.04+); never inside tmux, screen, CI or a dumb terminal.

TerminalSettings.description: How devlanes uses the terminal: its progress bar, tab title, links, notifications and marks.
TerminalSettings.markdownDescription: How devlanes uses the terminal: its progress bar, tab title, links, notifications and marks.

links.description: Whether service URLs, config error locations and log or bundle paths are clickable links (the OSC 8 sequence); defaults to `auto`, which writes them in iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm, Ghostty, Windows Terminal, VTE terminals, Konsole, Alacritty and foot. Elsewhere the same text prints without a link. `DEVLANES_TERM_LINKS=0` or `1` overrides this setting.
links.markdownDescription: Whether service URLs, config error locations and log or bundle paths are clickable links (the OSC 8 sequence); defaults to `auto`, which writes them in iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm, Ghostty, Windows Terminal, VTE terminals, Konsole, Alacritty and foot. Elsewhere the same text prints without a link. `DEVLANES_TERM_LINKS=0` or `1` overrides this setting.

marks.description: Whether long command output (logs of several services, failed starts) marks where each section starts, so the terminal's jump-to-mark or jump-to-prompt keys move between them; defaults to `auto`: marks in iTerm2, and prompt marks (OSC 133) in WezTerm, Ghostty, kitty, foot and Windows Terminal. `DEVLANES_TERM_MARKS=0` or `1` overrides this setting.
marks.markdownDescription: Whether long command output (logs of several services, failed starts) marks where each section starts, so the terminal's jump-to-mark or jump-to-prompt keys move between them; defaults to `auto`: marks in iTerm2, and prompt marks (OSC 133) in WezTerm, Ghostty, kitty, foot and Windows Terminal. `DEVLANES_TERM_MARKS=0` or `1` overrides this setting.

notifications.description: Whether a start that took a while finishing or failing, and a running service crashing, show a desktop notification while the terminal is not focused; defaults to `auto`. The TUI knows focus from the terminal; a command such as `devlanes start` does not, so with `auto` it notifies only in kitty, which itself skips a focused window. Terminals without notifications get the bell. At most one notification per 10 seconds. `DEVLANES_TERM_NOTIFICATIONS=0` or `1` overrides this setting.
notifications.markdownDescription: Whether a start that took a while finishing or failing, and a running service crashing, show a desktop notification while the terminal is not focused; defaults to `auto`. The TUI knows focus from the terminal; a command such as `devlanes start` does not, so with `auto` it notifies only in kitty, which itself skips a focused window. Terminals without notifications get the bell. At most one notification per 10 seconds. `DEVLANES_TERM_NOTIFICATIONS=0` or `1` overrides this setting.

progress.description: Whether starts show their progress in the terminal tab's own progress bar (the OSC 9;4 sequence); defaults to `auto`. Only human output on a terminal gets it, and `DEVLANES_TERM_PROGRESS=0` or `1` overrides this setting.
progress.markdownDescription: Whether starts show their progress in the terminal tab's own progress bar (the OSC 9;4 sequence); defaults to `auto`. Only human output on a terminal gets it, and `DEVLANES_TERM_PROGRESS=0` or `1` overrides this setting.

title.description: Whether the terminal tab's title says what devlanes is doing (`devlanes · acme@0 · starting 3/8` in the TUI, `devlanes start acme@0 · 3/8` or `devlanes logs -f api` for long commands); defaults to `auto`. The previous title is saved on the terminal's title stack and put back on exit, so `auto` sets it only where that stack exists: xterm, iTerm2, kitty, Ghostty and VTE terminals such as GNOME Terminal. Never inside tmux or screen, which manage titles themselves. `DEVLANES_TERM_TITLE=0` or `1` overrides this setting.
title.markdownDescription: Whether the terminal tab's title says what devlanes is doing (`devlanes · acme@0 · starting 3/8` in the TUI, `devlanes start acme@0 · 3/8` or `devlanes logs -f api` for long commands); defaults to `auto`. The previous title is saved on the terminal's title stack and put back on exit, so `auto` sets it only where that stack exists: xterm, iTerm2, kitty, Ghostty and VTE terminals such as GNOME Terminal. Never inside tmux or screen, which manage titles themselves. `DEVLANES_TERM_TITLE=0` or `1` overrides this setting.

TlsConfig.description: Certificate authority behind the proxy's HTTPS certificates, and the stores `devlanes certs trust` installs it into.
TlsConfig.markdownDescription: Certificate authority behind the proxy's HTTPS certificates, and the stores `devlanes certs trust` installs it into.

ca.description: Which CA signs the certificate for each lane hostname; defaults to `devlanes`. Choose `mkcert` when your browsers already trust mkcert's CA.
ca.markdownDescription: Which CA signs the certificate for each lane hostname; defaults to `devlanes`. Choose `mkcert` when your browsers already trust mkcert's CA.

trust.description: Stores `devlanes certs trust` installs the CA into and `certs untrust` removes it from; an empty list means `[system]`. On Linux, browsers do not read the system store, so add `chrome` and `firefox` there; inside WSL add `windows` for browsers on Windows. `devlanes doctor` shows each store's state.

items.description: Certificate store that `devlanes certs trust` installs the CA into.
items.markdownDescription: Certificate store that `devlanes certs trust` installs the CA into.

trust.markdownDescription: Stores `devlanes certs trust` installs the CA into and `certs untrust` removes it from; an empty list means `[system]`. On Linux, browsers do not read the system store, so add `chrome` and `firefox` there; inside WSL add `windows` for browsers on Windows. `devlanes doctor` shows each store's state.

TrustTarget.description: Certificate store that `devlanes certs trust` installs the CA into.
enumDescriptions: The OS store: the login keychain on macOS, read by Safari, Chrome, Edge and `/usr/bin/curl`; on Linux, the distribution's CA anchors, updated through sudo.
Every Firefox profile's certificate database, through `certutil` from the NSS tools (`brew install nss`, or `libnss3-tools` / `nss-tools` on Linux).
The store Chrome and Chromium read: `~/.pki/nssdb` through `certutil` on Linux, the same login keychain as `system` on macOS.

The Windows user root store, read by Edge, Chrome and Firefox on Windows. For devlanes inside WSL, whose browser usually runs on Windows: it runs Windows' `certutil.exe` through interop, and Windows asks you to confirm each change. On Windows it is the same store as `system`; on macOS and Linux outside WSL `certs trust` reports it as unavailable.
Reserved for the iOS simulator; not supported yet, so it is dropped with a warning.
Reserved for the Android emulator; not supported yet, so it is dropped with a warning.

TuiConfig.description: Terminal UI settings: when it opens, its colors and symbols, and what quitting does with running lanes. Changes apply to the next command.
TuiConfig.markdownDescription: Terminal UI settings: when it opens, its colors and symbols, and what quitting does with running lanes. Changes apply to the next command.

glyphs.description: Characters the TUI draws states, markers and the spinner with; defaults to `auto`. Set `ascii` when your font shows boxes or misaligned symbols.
glyphs.markdownDescription: Characters the TUI draws states, markers and the spinner with; defaults to `auto`. Set `ascii` when your font shows boxes or misaligned symbols.

on_quit.description: What `q` or Ctrl+C does while lanes of the project on screen are running; defaults to `ask`. Ticking "remember" in the quit dialog writes the choice here.
on_quit.markdownDescription: What `q` or Ctrl+C does while lanes of the project on screen are running; defaults to `ask`. Ticking "remember" in the quit dialog writes the choice here.

open_on_start.description: Open the TUI for `start`, `restart`, `lane resume` and `lane new --start` when they run at a terminal; defaults to true. Set false to have them print text instead, as `--no-ui` or `DEVLANES_NO_UI=1` do.
open_on_start.markdownDescription: Open the TUI for `start`, `restart`, `lane resume` and `lane new --start` when they run at a terminal; defaults to true. Set false to have them print text instead, as `--no-ui` or `DEVLANES_NO_UI=1` do.

theme.description: Color palette of the TUI; defaults to `auto`, which picks one from what the terminal reports. Choose `dark` or `light` when auto guesses wrong; `NO_COLOR` in the environment turns colors off whatever this says.
theme.markdownDescription: Color palette of the TUI; defaults to `auto`, which picks one from what the terminal reports. Choose `dark` or `light` when auto guesses wrong; `NO_COLOR` in the environment turns colors off whatever this says.

TuiGlyphs.description: Character set the TUI draws its symbols with.
enumDescriptions: Unicode, or ASCII when the locale (the first of `LC_ALL`, `LC_CTYPE` and `LANG` that is set) is not UTF-8.
Always Unicode symbols, such as ● ✕ ▾ and a braille spinner.
Plain ASCII only, for fonts or terminals that draw Unicode symbols badly.
TuiGlyphs.markdownDescription: Character set the TUI draws its symbols with.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Unicode, or ASCII when the locale (the first of `LC_ALL`, `LC_CTYPE` and `LANG` that is set) is not UTF-8.
Always Unicode symbols, such as ● ✕ ▾ and a braille spinner.
Plain ASCII only, for fonts or terminals that draw Unicode symbols badly.

TuiOnQuit.description: What quitting the TUI does with the running lanes of the project on screen.
enumDescriptions: Show a dialog each time to choose between keeping the lanes running and stopping them.
Close the TUI at once; every lane keeps running in the daemon.
Stop the running lanes of the project on screen, then close the TUI. Lanes of other projects keep running.
TuiOnQuit.markdownDescription: What quitting the TUI does with the running lanes of the project on screen.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Show a dialog each time to choose between keeping the lanes running and stopping them.
Close the TUI at once; every lane keeps running in the daemon.
Stop the running lanes of the project on screen, then close the TUI. Lanes of other projects keep running.

enumDescriptions: Use the true-color dark or light palette when the terminal reports true color (`COLORTERM`) and its background (`COLORFGBG`); otherwise the terminal's 16 colors.
Always use the true-color palette made for a dark background.
Always use the true-color palette made for a light background.
Use only the terminal's 16 named colors, so the TUI follows the terminal's color scheme.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Use the true-color dark or light palette when the terminal reports true color (`COLORTERM`) and its background (`COLORFGBG`); otherwise the terminal's 16 colors.
Always use the true-color palette made for a dark background.

UpdatesConfig.description: Release checks: the daemon reads the latest release's version once a day and commands print a one-line notice. Nothing is downloaded or installed.
UpdatesConfig.markdownDescription: Release checks: the daemon reads the latest release's version once a day and commands print a one-line notice. Nothing is downloaded or installed.

check.description: Have the daemon read the latest release's version from GitHub once a day; when it is newer, commands print the upgrade command on one line, at most once a day. Defaults to true; `DEVLANES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` or a CI environment also turns it off.
check.markdownDescription: Have the daemon read the latest release's version from GitHub once a day; when it is newer, commands print the upgrade command on one line, at most once a day. Defaults to true; `DEVLANES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` or a CI environment also turns it off.

UserLanesConfig.description: Machine settings for lanes. Each lane gets its own data folder at `<data_dir>/<project>/<lane id>`, available as `${{ lane.data_path }}` and `DEVLANES_LANE_DATA`. devlanes creates it when the lane is created and before each start, and `devlanes lane clean` deletes it.
UserLanesConfig.markdownDescription: Machine settings for lanes. Each lane gets its own data folder at `<data_dir>/<project>/<lane id>`, available as `${{ lane.data_path }}` and `DEVLANES_LANE_DATA`. devlanes creates it when the lane is created and before each start, and `devlanes lane clean` deletes it.

data_dir.description: Folder that holds every lane's data folder, one subfolder per project; defaults to `data` in the devlanes home (`~/.devlanes/data`). Must be an absolute path or start with `~/`. The daemon reads it when it starts. After a change and a daemon restart, lanes use new, empty folders under the new root; move the old folders there by hand to keep their data.
data_dir.markdownDescription: Folder that holds every lane's data folder, one subfolder per project; defaults to `data` in the devlanes home (`~/.devlanes/data`). Must be an absolute path or start with `~/`. The daemon reads it when it starts. After a change and a daemon restart, lanes use new, empty folders under the new root; move the old folders there by hand to keep their data.

description: devlanes user config: per-user settings in ~/.devlanes/config.yaml. Run a dev environment per git worktree, side by side. https://devlanes.run
markdownDescription: devlanes user config: per-user settings in ~/.devlanes/config.yaml. Run a dev environment per git worktree, side by side. https://devlanes.run

daemon.description: The daemon's lifetime: whether it stops on its own once the last TUI closes and nothing runs.
daemon.markdownDescription: The daemon's lifetime: whether it stops on its own once the last TUI closes and nothing runs.

history.description: How long the database keeps records of finished service and task runs, and of remote boxes that no longer connect.
history.markdownDescription: How long the database keeps records of finished service and task runs, and of remote boxes that no longer connect.

hostnames.description: How lane hostnames such as `api.acme-2.localhost` resolve to this machine: the strategy (`resolver`), its `tld`, and whether names also go into `/etc/hosts` (`hosts_file`). The defaults need no setup for browsers that resolve `*.localhost`.
hostnames.markdownDescription: How lane hostnames such as `api.acme-2.localhost` resolve to this machine: the strategy (`resolver`), its `tld`, and whether names also go into `/etc/hosts` (`hosts_file`). The defaults need no setup for browsers that resolve `*.localhost`.

lanes.description: Where lane data folders (`lane.data_path`) live on this machine.
lanes.markdownDescription: Where lane data folders (`lane.data_path`) live on this machine.

logs.description: How much service output devlanes keeps under `~/.devlanes/logs`, by age and total size.
logs.markdownDescription: How much service output devlanes keeps under `~/.devlanes/logs`, by age and total size.

metrics.description: How long CPU and memory history stays in the daemon's database.
metrics.markdownDescription: How long CPU and memory history stays in the daemon's database.

ports.description: Port range that every lane of every project takes its block of ports from, so lanes never collide. Defaults to `20000-32767`.
ports.markdownDescription: Port range that every lane of every project takes its block of ports from, so lanes never collide. Defaults to `20000-32767`.

proxy.description: Ports of the daemon's HTTP/HTTPS proxy, which serves every `hosts` entry, and whether other devices on the network may connect to it.
proxy.markdownDescription: Ports of the daemon's HTTP/HTTPS proxy, which serves every `hosts` entry, and whether other devices on the network may connect to it.

start.description: What a plain `devlanes start` (no services, no `--profile`) brings up: the services the lane ran before, or its default selection.
start.markdownDescription: What a plain `devlanes start` (no services, no `--profile`) brings up: the services the lane ran before, or its default selection.

startup.description: How many services may be starting at the same time across all lanes and projects, so a large start does not overload the machine. Defaults to one start per CPU core.
startup.markdownDescription: How many services may be starting at the same time across all lanes and projects, so a large start does not overload the machine. Defaults to one start per CPU core.

state.description: Size budget for the daemon's database; past it, the oldest metrics and history are deleted before their retention ends.
state.markdownDescription: Size budget for the daemon's database; past it, the oldest metrics and history are deleted before their retention ends.

terminal.description: Terminal integration of the CLI, written as a mapping with `progress` (the tab's progress bar during starts). A plain string, the terminal app name older versions used, is still accepted but ignored with a warning.
terminal.markdownDescription: Terminal integration of the CLI, written as a mapping with `progress` (the tab's progress bar during starts). A plain string, the terminal app name older versions used, is still accepted but ignored with a warning.

tls.description: Which certificate authority signs the proxy's HTTPS certificates (`ca`), and which stores `devlanes certs trust` installs it into (`trust`).
tls.markdownDescription: Which certificate authority signs the proxy's HTTPS certificates (`ca`), and which stores `devlanes certs trust` installs it into (`trust`).

tui.description: Whether start commands open the terminal UI, how it looks, and what quitting it does with running lanes.
tui.markdownDescription: Whether start commands open the terminal UI, how it looks, and what quitting it does with running lanes.

updates.description: Daily check for a newer devlanes release; nothing is downloaded or installed.
updates.markdownDescription: Daily check for a newer devlanes release; nothing is downloaded or installed.
